summary.text: Liz Thomson, listed by Ballotpedia as Elizabeth Thomson, is a Democratic state representative from New Mexico House District 24 who took office in 2017 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
A retired pediatric physical therapist, Thomson chairs the House Health & Human Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Thomson earned a high school diploma from Crownpoint High School and a bachelor's degree in physical therapy from the University of New Mexico in 1984, and her professional experience includes working as a physical therapist.

In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, Thomson said she spent more than 35 years working with children from birth to age 22 who have or are at risk of developing disabilities, and that she has served on numerous nonprofit and public boards, including the NM Autism Society and the NM Developmental Disabilities Council.
In the 2025-2026 session, Thomson chairs the House Health & Human Services Committee and serves on the Consumer & Public Affairs Committee.

In the survey, Thomson said she has served 12 years in the House, previously chaired the House Consumer and Public Affairs Committee, and spent four years on the House Appropriations and Finance Committee.

Thomson listed her key messages as making health care accessible and affordable for all, giving a voice to children, people with disabilities, women and people living in poverty, and treating budgets as moral documents.
